key_insight: HP-RLVR assigns token-level credit from a single rollout by comparing a model’s present-token view with a hindsight view of the realized future, avoiding group sampling while keeping reward signal even on failed attempts.
engineering_relevance: For scalable RLVR training, this offers a lower-rollout, no-critic alternative that can improve throughput and preserve usable gradients when many sampled attempts would otherwise collapse to the same terminal reward.
method: Single-rollout RLVR with token-level weighting from hindsight context
Compute a normalized Jensen–Shannon divergence between causal and hindsight token views
Use the divergence to weight reward relative to a historical baseline, with no reference solution or learned critic
evidence_signal: On paired Qwen3-8B runs over a shared 100-step schedule, HP-RLVR was 1.21×, 1.46×, and 2.30× faster than GRPO on math, code generation, and ALFWorld using one-eighth the rollouts per prompt, with comparable overall accuracy and zero gradient records absent in HP-RLVR.
watch_item: The method depends on the generating policy snapshot and hindsight verifier feedback, so implementation quality and stability of the hindsight weighting may be sensitive to verifier design and task type.
paper_title: Hindsight-Privileged RLVR: Single-Rollout Token Credit Without Group Sampling
